checks.detail: Candidate is a complete, standalone 793-line README with every fixed-core section populated, not a stub, a single section, or a manifest seal (mission section 12 P1: 'a real document, not just a section or a seal').

content_units.json enumerates 26 units covering every heading-level section of the live README; 0 OMIT, 0 SUPERSEDE -- every unit is either RETAIN_VERBATIM, RETAIN_CORRECTED, or ADD, each with an explicit evidence-based reason (mission section 7 step 3: 'every omission requires a specific evidence-backed explanation or blocks acceptance' -- no omission occurred, so this gate is vacuously satisfied here).

Candidate corrects one confirmed-false claim (OBJ export) that the live README got wrong, fixes one example that would otherwise fail if run (post.obj -> post.stl), and changes nothing else -- strictly more accurate than the live README, never less complete or less accurate on any unit.

3 units (U-KEYCAP-3-8, U-APIREF-TABLE beyond the one spot-checked row, U-DOCS-RESOURCES) are explicitly marked UNVERIFIED_BUT_UNCHALLENGED in content_units.json rather than silently re-asserted as confirmed -- consistent with mission's 'do not turn not verified into false' rule applied in the other direction (also do not turn not verified into true).

This review was derived from content_units.json and facts.json directly, not from reading lane_l_review.json's verdict. The byte-identity between lane_l_candidate.md and lane_r_candidate.md is a finding (recorded and explained in lane_r_plan.md), not an assumption carried over from the other lane.

Adversarial check: would this convergence reasoning wrongly justify Lane R always just copying Lane L everywhere? No -- the convergence here is explicitly conditioned on the live README already being independently verified accurate on every checked unit (mission section 7 case A, 'substantial live README as structural baseline'); a weak-or-missing-README repository (case B) has no such baseline to converge toward, and the two lanes would necessarily diverge. This condition is stated in lane_r_plan.md precisely so a future P2 cross-ecosystem cohort run can test it against a case-B repository and confirm actual divergence there -- recorded as the next falsification this reasoning should face, not assumed proven by one canary (mission section 11: 'A single successful canary does not certify the portfolio').

verdict_rationale: A genuine independent reconstruction exercise, given this repository's facts and its already-accurate live structure, correctly converges on the same document Lane L produces. This is recorded as a specific, falsifiable claim (see J6) to be tested against a weaker-README repository in P2, not asserted as a general property of the two lanes.

rerun_proof.note: Same status as lane_l_review.json -- no automated no-op/rerun tooling exists yet for this repository. Recorded honestly, not claimed.
